docs/research-r3/02-research-gaps.md:7:Use a retained **semantic widget tree** (stable widget IDs, parent/child, bounds, role/name/value/state/actions) and a per-frame immediate **paint command stream**. This gives stable focus/accessibility/undo/event identity without requiring retained GPU objects. Default layout is flexbox-like constraints with a single top-down measure/arrange pass plus bounded second pass for intrinsic text. Clay is a useful small C reference for declarative layout, but not the whole UI. Dear ImGui docking and Nuklear show immediate widget patterns; they do not solve accessibility/IME for this product. RAD Debugger, GPUI, Flutter and Makepad are architecture references only. [Clay](https://github.com/nicbarker/clay) [Dear ImGui docking](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/wiki/Docking) [Nuklear](https://github.com/Immediate-Mode-UI/Nuklear) [Flutter architecture](https://docs.flutter.dev/resources/architectural-overview) [GPUI](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/tree/main/crates/gpui)
docs/research-r3/02-research-gaps.md:9:Minimum widget set: app/menu bar and commands; dockable split panes; tabs; layer/object virtual tree; property inspector; color picker; numeric fields with keyboard entry and drag scrubbing; slider; checkbox/radio/dropdown; context menu; tooltip; searchable command palette; text field with selection, clipboard and IME; scroll views with trackpad momentum; dialogs delegated to OS; canvas and selection handles. Virtual lists use visible rows + overscan and stable IDs, so one million XML/layer rows allocate O(viewport rows), not O(N) widget objects. Docking should start as fixed panes with draggable splitters, defer arbitrary tear-off docking.
docs/research-r3/02-research-gaps.md:11:Architecture details: central command registry (ID, label, shortcut, enabled predicate, execute callback, undo policy); keyboard routing: text input → focused widget → modal → focused panel → document/tool commands → app; pointer capture per pointer ID; gesture arena resolves drag vs click vs pan; event positions are logical points, convert once to physical pixels. Property edits open one undo transaction at pointer-down/focus, update preview on motion, commit once on release/Enter, cancel on Escape. DnD has typed MIME payloads and hover/drop targets. Tooltips delayed (~450 ms proposed), animations use monotonic clock and easing; respect reduced-motion preference. Localization: UTF-8, message catalog, plural rules, no concatenated sentences; RTL requires mirrored layout and bidi text, so do not assume just translating labels.

The earliest complete Rust desktop requires an audited Apple binding boundary, native shell, Core Text adapter, Metal presentation, and a small integration executable. Existing system wrappers do not provide AppKit integration.

Reviewed OWNER-DIRECTIVES, AGENTS, frozen native-plan and owned-document orders; named window/text/Metal headers; native shell, window events, geometry, text and presentation implementation excerpts; Rust UI/document contracts; and existing platform/toolchain research. Owned-document candidate code was not consumed.

**Proposed API contracts**

- `MainThread::acquire() -> Result<MainThread, PlatformError>` verifies Apple’s main thread. `NativeApp`, `Window`, menus, preference subscriptions, accessibility objects and presenters are `!Send + !Sync`; their operations require this capability. `NativeApp::start`, `create_window`, `run` and `shutdown` define one application lifecycle, regular activation, launch completion and autorelease pools around native turns.
- `WindowConfig` validates UTF-8, rejects embedded NUL, preserves the 1,024-byte title and 1–4,096-point dimensions. Fallible creation publishes no partially initialized handle. Public types expose no Objective-C pointers.
- `WindowId { slot, generation }` identifies callback targets. Retained native objects belong to platform owners; delegates, observers and completion blocks use invalidatable weak routing state. Callbacks enqueue owned events, never hold application-model borrows or invoke application mutation reentrantly. No Rust panic crosses Objective-C/C/block boundaries: catch unwind where supported, mark failure and request orderly shutdown; document abort behavior separately. Native exceptions must never unwind through Rust.
- `Event` separates key transitions, modifiers, committed text and composition updates. Implement `NSTextInputClient` for marked text, selection and candidate positioning; `charactersIgnoringModifiers` alone is insufficient. Translate modifier bits explicitly: C platform and accepted Rust UI constants differ.
- Preserve finite top-left point coordinates, precise scroll/magnification, monotonic timestamps and separate backing-pixel dimensions. Geometry conversion remains per-window/per-display. The accepted canvas permits integer backing scales 1–3; reject unsupported scales explicitly pending an accepted adaptation.
- Use a bounded 256-event queue with owned UTF-8/path payloads and typed overflow. Coalesce adjacent compatible motion/resize events without crossing key/button/command barriers. Reserve control capacity; saturation latches an observable fault and resets input state instead of silently losing releases or close requests. Bound native dispatch per turn; sleep/wake through the run loop.
- `FontService::layout(TextRequest) -> Result<TextLayout, TextError>` borrows inputs only during calls and returns owned metrics/outlines. Preserve media limits: 64-KiB text, 16,384 glyphs, 262,144 segments, 32 families, normal/italic/oblique, and unsupported color glyphs. Rust UI: 128 nodes/depth24, 63-byte previews/1-MiB total strings, 127-byte drafts/63-byte labels; C labels use normal style/400-or-600 weight. No 4,000-codepoint fallback exists in inspected sources. Main-thread-owned label rendering implements accepted `TextDraw`, retaining no text/pixel borrow; validate stride, clipping and lengths. Preserve the 64-entry/4-MiB cache bound.
- `Presenter::present(&RgbaFrame) -> Result<Submission, PresentError>` copies borrowed pixels before return. Per-window textures avoid legacy global resource coupling; bounded in-flight submissions retain GPU resources until completion. Freeze channel/alpha semantics, checked sizes and the 8,192-axis limit. Drawable absence is recoverable; readback verification stays separate.
- Menus consume command descriptors/state snapshots and emit typed commands once. AX consumes validated owned `SemanticsSnapshot`s, converts frames to screen coordinates and routes actions by window generation. Preference watching returns a removable subscription.
- Teardown invalidates routing first, cancels sheets/timers/jobs, unregisters observers and AX/menu targets, detaches delegates, retires GPU submissions, clears caches, releases windows, then stops AppKit. Late completions discard stale generations.

**Hard dependencies and proposed work orders**

1. **NATIVE-BINDINGS:** coordinator-approved dependency ADR/provenance and macOS-13 symbol audit. objc2 remains a proposal. Evaluate only required objc2/Foundation/AppKit/CoreFoundation/CoreGraphics/CoreText/Metal/QuartzCore features; justify block support separately, defer dispatch bindings. Before fetch/adoption, verify current primary manifests, exact pins, checksums, transitive licenses, SDK-derived provenance, compiler compatibility and callback APIs. Existing research establishes neither newest versions nor verified licenses.
2. **NATIVE-SHELL:** map `platform_window*.m`, native-shell/internal headers and geometry into startup, windows, responder/input, queues and teardown.
3. **NATIVE-TEXT-PRESENT:** map both text implementations and Metal/shaders into font/draw/presenter contracts.
4. **NATIVE-MENU-AX:** map menu and accessibility implementations, command routing and preferences.
5. **DESKTOP-CHECKPOINT:** bundle executable/resources; connect accepted custom UI to these seams. First usable GUI: labeled interactive custom canvas, keyboard/IME, resize/scale, menus, VoiceOver and clean close.

Document opening additionally requires accepted owned-document APIs: immutable `Arc<Vec<u8>>`, offset spans, cancellation and generation-tagged bounded job results. No self-referential borrowed model.

MacOS-26 material branches require availability guards; macOS-13 compatibility remains unverified. All first-party implementation stays Rust behind platform interfaces: custom UI, owned SVG, no C shims, GPL source or unsupported-OS backends.

## Ownership, thread and foreign boundaries

Published `MainThreadMarker::new() -> Option<Self>` uses Apple's
`pthread_main_np`; its marker is `!Send + !Sync`. NSApplication inherits the
main-thread responder boundary. Acquire the capability safely; do not use
`new_unchecked` to bypass it. Keep application/window/menu/AX/preferences/
presenter owners main-thread confined even where framework types are permissive.

`Retained<T>` retains/releases Objective-C ownership; `CFRetained<T>` owns CF
Create results. Get-returned objects remain borrowed or must be retained before
escaping. Platform wrappers expose no native pointers. Delegates/observers/
blocks route by invalidatable window generation. Callbacks copy bounded owned
UTF-8/path events, never retain model/pixel borrows or mutate the model
reentrantly. Preserve the 256-event queue/fault policy, accepted scale limits,
text/glyph/path/cache bounds and checked RGBA sizes. IME requires complete
NSTextInputClient requirements and UTF-16 range conversion; legacy
charactersIgnoringModifiers is insufficient.

Block2 is justified by asynchronous sheets, notification/timer observers and
MTLCommandBuffer completion. `RcBlock::new` copies captures to heap; clone uses
_Block_copy. Heap copying does not extend borrowed captures. Use owned captures
and explicit lifetime/invalidation. Published blocks do not enforce every
cross-thread capture condition: Metal completion captures must be thread-safe,
without UI markers or model borrows. Completion only updates bounded retained
submission state; main-thread UI observes owned results. CGPathApply needs no
block. Copy frame bytes before returning; retain in-flight GPU resources, tolerate
missing drawables, and separate readback verification.

Rust panic handling and Objective-C exceptions are distinct. Published objc2
`catch-all` activates `exception`, wrapping message sends and converting caught
Objective-C exceptions to Rust panics. Explicit `exception::catch` returns an
exception result while Rust panics continue. Both require the published helper:
its build.rs uses cc/Clang, `-xobjective-c`, `-fobjc-exceptions`, without ARC;
`try_catch.m` catches Objective-C objects, retains them and lets Rust/C++ unwinds
continue. This is third-party Objective-C, not an authorized first-party shim.
Adoption must explicitly accept this native build dependency and audit its
complete provenance/closure. No pure-Rust foreign-exception fence is established.

Catch Rust unwinds inside every inbound callback, latch failure and return an
ABI-valid fallback; never unwind into AppKit/C/block callers. Panic=abort cannot
provide recovery. Catch-all is not a guarantee against exceptions from raw C
calls, retain/release, cleanup or exceptional exception handling, and the helper
uses a Rust C-unwind trampoline internally. The proposal's absolute prohibition
on foreign unwinding through Rust therefore needs an explicit boundary decision;
catch_unwind alone cannot satisfy it. Legacy KVO @try/@catch cannot simply be
removed. Teardown invalidates routing, cancels sheets/timers, unregisters
observers, detaches delegates and retires GPU resources before object release.

```rust
pub struct NativeApp { /* private, !Send + !Sync */ }
pub struct Window { /* private retained AppKit owner, !Send + !Sync */ }
pub struct WindowId { pub slot: u32, pub generation: u32 }
pub struct WindowConfig { pub title: String, pub width_points: u32,
    pub height_points: u32, pub resizable: bool, pub initially_hidden: bool }
pub enum WindowEvent { Open, Focus(bool), Resize{points: Size, pixels: SizeU32},
    BackingScaleChanged{scale: f64, pixels: SizeU32}, KeyDown{code:u16, modifiers:Modifiers},
    KeyUp{code:u16, modifiers:Modifiers}, Pointer(PointerEvent), Scroll(ScrollEvent),
    Magnify{at:Point, amount:f64}, TextCommitted(String), Composition(Composition),
    CloseRequested, AnimationTick{monotonic_seconds:f64}, QueueFault(QueueFault) }
pub fn NativeApp::start(mt: MainThread) -> Result<Self, WindowError>;
pub fn NativeApp::create_window(&mut self, config: WindowConfig)
    -> Result<(WindowId, Window), WindowError>;
pub fn Window::set_title(&mut self, title: String) -> Result<(), WindowError>;
pub fn Window::set_visible(&mut self, visible: bool) -> Result<(), WindowError>;
pub fn Window::resize(&mut self, size: Size) -> Result<(), WindowError>;
pub fn Window::content_screen_origin(&self) -> Result<Point, WindowError>;
pub fn Window::set_cursor(&mut self, cursor: Cursor) -> Result<(), WindowError>;
pub fn Window::request_ticks(&mut self, enabled: bool) -> Result<(), WindowError>;
pub fn NativeApp::poll_events(&mut self, window: WindowId, max: NonZeroUsize)
    -> Result<Vec<WindowEvent>, WindowError>;
pub fn Window::destroy(self) -> Result<(), WindowError>;
pub fn NativeApp::shutdown(self) -> Result<(), WindowError>;

Every public native operation takes/retains the capability through its owner. `NativeApp`, `Window`, subscriptions, and route state are main-thread-only. Reject nonintegral or out-of-range backing scale until the accepted UI contract is extended (UI currently accepts integer 1..=3).

Allowed production additions: `rust/crates/vexel-platform-apple/src/native_window/{mod.rs,types.rs,app.rs,window.rs,geometry.rs,input.rs,ime.rs,queue.rs,ticks.rs,teardown.rs}` and a single `mod native_window`/re-export addition to that crate'"'s "'`src/lib.rs`. **Startup/window:** `NativeApp::start` acquires shared `NSApplication`, regular activation policy, finish launch, and establishes main run-loop ownership. `create_window` validates all fields before native allocation; on any native failure, release partial objects and publish no handle. UI `TextEdit` uses UTF-8 byte offsets; do conversion explicitly and preserve composition selection.
